statement: The dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
why: One dollar buys nearly 160 yen, even after Japan's government spent close to 100 billion dollars buying yen to prop it up. In a Reuters poll, 86 in 100 economists expect the Bank of Japan to raise its interest rate to 1.50% at its meeting on December 17-18, and its governor, Kazuo Ueda, says the bank should keep raising. A higher rate, a government ready to buy yen again and a nervous stock market all tend to make the yen stronger. We are wrong if one dollar buys more yen at year end than on November 20, for example because the Bank of Japan does not raise its rate, or because a US rate rise makes the dollar more attractive.

statement: Bitcoin will be cheaper on December 4, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
why: Bitcoin has fallen six weeks in a row and dipped below 62,000 dollars. Investors keep pulling money out of US bitcoin funds, and an expected US interest rate rise plus falling stock prices make people avoid risky bets. We expect the slide to go on for two more weeks. We are wrong if bitcoin costs more on December 4 than on November 20, for example because the steep fall tempts bargain hunters, or money starts flowing back into the bitcoin funds.

statement: Brent crude oil will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026, when a barrel closed near 92.57 dollars.
why: The price of Brent oil fell 4 in 100 last week, as tankers sailed through the Strait of Hormuz in about the same numbers as before the war. In October a barrel cost more than 116 dollars. The Middle East is pumping more oil, and falling stock prices hint that people and businesses will use less. We are wrong if a barrel costs more at year end than on November 20, for example because new attacks in the Iran war stop the tankers again, or OPEC+, the group of big oil producers, decides to pump less at its meeting on November 29.
